question: What is the documentation difference between engineering judgment and an engineering study in the MUTCD definitions?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The key documentation difference is that engineering judgment does not have to be documented, while an engineering study must be documented in writing. Per the definitions shown in the glossary (Section 1C.02), both must be exercised/performed by a professional engineer (or an individual working under the supervision of such an engineer), but only the engineering study carries a written documentation requirement. This matters in practice: a deviation from a Standard provision is allowed only where the agency fully documents the engineering basis through an engineering study. Standards (mandatory): - From the glossary definition of Engineering Judgment: "Documentation of engineering judgment is not required." [Image 5] - From the glossary definition of Engineering Study: "An engineering study shall be performed by a professional engineer (see definition in this Section) with appropriate traffic engineering expertise, or by an individual working under the supervision of such an engineer... An engineering study shall be documented in writing." [Image 5] - "Where the content of this Manual requires a decision for implementation, such decisions shall be made by an engineer, or an individual under the supervision of an engineer... Those decisions shall be made using engineering judgment or engineering study, as required by the MUTCD provision." - "In limited, location-specific cases, the results of a documented engineering study (see Section 1D.03) might indicate a deviation from one or more requirements of a Standard provision to be appropriate." Support (informational): - "Definitions of professional engineer, engineering study, and engineering judgment are provided in Section 1C.02." - "Site-specific conditions might result in the determination that it is impossible or impracticable to comply with a Standard at that location... In such limited, specific cases, the deviation is allowed, provided that the agency or official having jurisdiction fully documents, through an engineering study, the engineering basis for the deviation." — i.e., undocumented engineering judgment is not sufficient to deviate from a Standard; a documented engineering study is required. - Similarly, agencies can install a traffic control signal where no warrants are met "but only after conducting an engineering study that documents the rationale" for the decision. Visual evidence: [Image 5] shows the glossary definitions (items 76 and 77), where engineering judgment expressly states "Documentation of engineering judgment is not required" and engineering study states "An engineering study shall be documented in writing." [Image 7] shows Section 1D.03, which explains that deviations from Standards are allowed only when the agency fully documents the engineering basis through an engineering study. Citations: - Section 1D.03 Support §1 (p.32) - Section 1D.03 Support §2 (p.32) - Section 1A.04 Standard §2 (p.2) - Section 1C.01 Standard §1 (p.13) - Section 4C.01 Support §20 (p.653) - Page 58 - Page 73
gold_answer: Both involve evaluating pertinent information and applying engineering principles by a professional engineer or a person under such an engineer's supervision. Engineering judgment does not require documentation; an engineering study must be documented in writing.
